A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KiVA study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison across renamed stages and relocated KiVA-adults material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model and human experiments on KiVA and KiVA-adults, including accuracy, standard errors, and human response-time analyses in Sections 4-5 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: V2 reports original human and model evaluations, including GPT-o1, no-change controls, verbal-question ablations, and a vision-only model experiment in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The proposed three-stage procedure remains unchanged: identify the transformation domain, specify the rule conditional on correct identification, and assess visual extrapolation independently. Verbal Classification and Verbal Specification rename existing stages. Added comparator models and experimental controls do not establish a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions already evaluate 1,400 KiVA and 2,900 KiVA-adults transformations across the same five domains; v2's 4,300-item abstract does not represent newly added coverage. V2 adds no-change scenarios and changes participant age coverage from children aged 3-7 to 3-5 and adults aged 21-35 to 21-40. KiVA-compositionality is announced without reported evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 adds GPT-o1 to both principal benchmark comparisons alongside GPT-4V, LLaVA-1.5, MANTIS, and humans. Appendix B.4 additionally evaluates a language-free Large Vision Model. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated model families.

E3.justification: The main KiVA human study changes from 40 adults and 20 children to 250 adults and 42 children, with 3-13 adult annotations per trial. Child-specific prompts replace v1's stated shared prompts. New protocols include 10% samples for no-change and supplied-answer controls, and visual-only testing with another 200 adults and 20 children. Figure 4 also introduces comparisons on child-annotated subsets.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained prompting experiments, v2 adds no-change controls, repeated-response consistency analysis, accuracy conditional on preceding reasoning, interventions supplying correct preceding answers, and removal of verbal questions. Appendix B.1 also examines single versus multiple images for GPT-o1, whereas v1 reported this comparison for GPT-4V. These analyses substantially expand investigation of failure sources.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging and standard-error bars remain; an increased model run count is not reported. However, v1 Figure 6 provides numerical correlation coefficients and p-values, while the replacement correlations in v2 Figure 7 provide neither. This reduces quantitative statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive GPT-o1, vision-only, and control results, including systematic false change detection by LLaVA-1.5 and MANTIS on no-change trials. KiVA human results use revised cohorts, and GPT-o1 correlations replace the earlier GPT-4V analyses. V1's single-image GPT-4V benchmark entries are no longer reported. Changed human scores are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops mathematical theorems or proofs. V2's expanded conceptual definition of analogy, renamed stages, and removal of some symbolic notation do not introduce substantive mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The principal contribution remains a developmentally motivated benchmark exposing visual analogy weaknesses. V2 changes the strongest-tested-model claim from GPT-4V to GPT-o1 and narrows the introductory claim of falling below children specifically to number and reflection. It also announces KiVA-compositionality as a further extension.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning verbal scaffolding, visual binding, failure despite supplied correct rules, and reasoning without language. It explicitly cautions that similar human-model performance patterns do not imply identical mechanisms. V1's explicit limitation that the benchmark does not capture the full spectrum of visual cognition is omitted.

D1.justification: V2 adds temperature and token-limit settings, detailed child instructions, explicit self-reflection prompts, and the vision-only model's perplexity-based answer selection. It also reports transformation-generation and compositionality code. These extend existing reproducibility documentation; some KiVA-adults sampling details, including the numerical-ambiguity constraint in v1 Appendix C.1, are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting visual binding, recent spatial/counting failures, developmental reasoning, and possible symbolic/Bayesian approaches, including Campbell, Coates, Goddu, and Depeweg. The central positioning against abstract-grid benchmarks remains stable. Bai's conference and preprint citations concern the same work rather than a new research contribution.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: KiVA-adults moves into the main benchmark description, Results and Discussion become subsections of Section 4, and the appendices are restructured around additional analyses. Stage terminology changes throughout, and the introduction, procedural explanations, and discussion receive substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned to show both benchmarks, performance plots are reorganized into direct human-model comparisons, and numerous diagnostic plots are added. V1's five separate appendix examples become v2 Figure 10, while numerical Tables 1 and 4 disappear. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation through broader human coverage and controls testing absent changes, verbal scaffolding, and failure despite correct preceding answers (Section 4 and Appendix B). These address important explanations left largely untested in v1. The gains outweigh reduced numerical and statistical detail and a new interpretation mismatch: Appendix B.4 emphasizes color and size, although Figure 14b places number above size.
